title: Stationary Drop Punt
objective: Develop a technically sound stationary drop punt by teaching correct ball drop, body position, foot contact and follow-through before introducing movement or defensive pressure.
players:
Minimum: 2
Ideal: 10–20
Maximum: Unlimited (working in pairs)
setup:
• Players work in pairs facing each other.
• Players should stand:
• Under 8–10: 8–10 metres apart.
• Under 12–14: 10–15 metres apart.
• Under 16 and above: 15–20 metres apart.
• Spread pairs evenly across the training area to prevent footballs crossing into neighbouring groups.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A begins with the football.
2. Player A performs a stationary drop punt to Player B.
3. Player B marks or gathers the football.
4. Player B resets before returning the kick.
5. Continue for the nominated time.
6. Swap the preferred kicking foot after several minutes if appropriate.
7. Players should prioritise correct technique rather than kicking distance.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Hold the football correctly.
Guide the ball onto the boot rather than throwing it.
Keep their head over the football.
Strike the ball with the laces of the boot.
Finish balanced.
Follow through directly towards the target.
Encourage smooth, controlled kicking rather than maximum power.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Provide one coaching correction before allowing several repetitions.

commonErrors.error: Throwing the ball onto the boot
commonErrors.correction: Guide the football gently from the hands.
Keep the chest over the football.
Finish balanced on the kicking foot.

commonErrors.error: Looking at the target too early
commonErrors.correction: Watch the football until contact.
Finish with the kicking leg pointing towards the target.

regressions: Allow players to stop and reset after every kick.
Slow the pace of the activity.
Demonstrate the technique again before restarting.
successIndicators: Maintain balance throughout the kicking action.
matchApplication: The drop punt is the primary kicking technique used throughout Australian Football. This drill develops the technical foundation required for: Maintaining possession. Passing to teammates. Kicking inside 50. Defensive exits. Goal kicking. General field kicking. Every advanced kicking drill in the AFCRL builds upon the skills developed in KK-001.

title: Stationary Drop Punt Gates
objective: Develop kicking accuracy by teaching players to consistently execute a drop punt through a defined target gate while maintaining correct kicking technique. This drill reinforces the importance of accuracy before increasing kicking distance or introducing movement.
players:
Minimum: 2
Ideal: 10–20
Maximum: Unlimited (working in pairs)
equipment: Additional cones to separate pairs if required.
setup:
• Players work in pairs facing each other.
• Place two cones approximately 1 metre apart halfway between each pair to create a kicking gate.
• Player spacing should be:
• Under 8–10: 8–10 metres apart.
• Under 12–14: 10–15 metres apart.
• Under 16 and above: 15–20 metres apart.
• Ensure enough space exists between pairs to avoid footballs crossing into neighbouring groups.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A begins with the football.
2. Player A performs a stationary drop punt towards Player B.
3. The football must pass cleanly through the cone gate before reaching Player B.
4. Player B marks or gathers the football.
5. Player B resets before returning the kick through the same gate.
6. Continue for the allocated time.
7. Coaches may award one point for every kick that travels cleanly through the gate without touching a cone.
8. The emphasis should remain on correct kicking technique rather than scoring points.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Maintain the same technique used in KK-001.
Keep the hips and shoulders aligned with the target.
Guide the football directly onto the kicking foot.
Strike through the centre of the football.
Finish with the kicking foot pointing towards the target.
Stay balanced after the kick.
Remind players that a smooth, technically correct kick is more important than a powerful kick.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the football travels through the gate.
Provide one coaching correction before allowing the player several opportunities to practise the adjustment.

commonErrors.error: Missing the gate to the left
commonErrors.correction: Finish with the kicking leg pointing directly at the target.

commonErrors.error: Missing the gate to the right
commonErrors.correction: Ensure hips and shoulders remain square to the target.
Focus on a smoother ball drop and straighter follow-through.
Reduce effort and concentrate on accuracy.
Guide the football onto the boot rather than throwing it.

progressions: Complete the drill using the non-preferred foot.
Reduce the preparation time before kicking.
regressions: Allow players to stop and reset before every kick.
Demonstrate the technique again before restarting.
successIndicators: Kick the football through the gate.
Demonstrate improved accuracy over successive attempts.
matchApplication: During a match, players are frequently required to pass the football through narrow spaces between opponents. This drill develops the accuracy required to identify and execute those kicks while maintaining sound drop punt technique.

title: Partner Accuracy Challenge
objective: Develop the ability to consistently deliver the football to a teammate's advantage by improving kicking accuracy, control and judgement of kicking weight. Players learn that an effective pass is one that allows the receiver to mark or gather the football with minimal movement.
players:
Minimum: 2
Ideal: 10–20
Maximum: Unlimited (working in pairs)
setup:
• Players work in pairs facing each other.
• Players should stand:
• Under 8–10: 8–10 metres apart.
• Under 12–14: 10–15 metres apart.
• Under 16 and above: 15–20 metres apart.
• Each pair should have sufficient space to kick safely without interfering with neighbouring groups.
• The receiving player should remain stationary throughout the drill.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A kicks to Player B.
2. The objective is to deliver the football directly to Player B's chest without requiring them to move their feet.
3. Player B marks or gathers the football.
4. Player B immediately returns the kick using the same objective.
5. Continue for the allocated time.
6. Coaches may introduce a simple scoring system:
7. 2 points for a chest mark.
8. 1 point if the receiver gathers the football cleanly after one bounce.
9. 0 points if the receiver must move significantly or the football misses the target.
10. The emphasis should remain on quality rather than competition.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Look at the target before beginning the kicking action.
Kick to where the receiver can comfortably mark the football.
Match the force of the kick to the required distance.
Maintain the same drop punt technique regardless of distance.
Stay balanced throughout the kicking action.
Finish towards the intended target.
Players should understand that kicking accurately is more important than kicking hard.
coachingCues: "Kick to your teammate, not at them."
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the receiver is forced to move.
Encourage players to evaluate each kick before receiving coaching feedback.

commonErrors.correction: Finish directly towards the target.
Reduce the height of the ball drop and maintain a flatter trajectory.
Reduce leg speed and focus on control.
Complete the follow-through and accelerate through the football.
Encourage the kicker to visualise the exact landing point before kicking.

regressions: Encourage players to stop and reset after each kick.
successIndicators: Deliver the football directly to the receiver.
Require minimal movement from the receiver.
Demonstrate good judgement of kicking weight.
Improve accuracy over the duration of the drill.
matchApplication: Most possessions in Australian Football involve passing to a teammate under little or no pressure. This drill develops the fundamental ability to consistently hit a teammate's preferred side, allowing the next possession to be completed quickly and efficiently.

title: Distance Progression
objective: Develop a player's ability to vary the distance of a drop punt while maintaining consistent kicking technique. Players learn to adjust the power of the kick without changing the mechanics of the skill.
players:
Minimum: 2
Ideal: 10–20
Maximum: Unlimited (working in pairs)
setup:
• Players work in pairs.
• Mark four kicking distances using cones.
• Recommended distances:
• Under 10: 10 m, 15 m, 20 m, 25 m
• Under 12–14: 15 m, 20 m, 25 m, 30 m
• Under 16 and above: 20 m, 30 m, 40 m, 50 m
• Players begin at the shortest distance.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Players complete five accurate kicks from the first distance.
2. Once successful, both players move back to the next marker.
3. Continue progressing until the maximum distance is reached.
4. If technique deteriorates significantly, return to the previous successful distance before attempting the longer kick again.
5. Players should never sacrifice technique simply to complete a longer kick.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Use exactly the same kicking mechanics regardless of distance.
Generate additional distance by increasing leg speed rather than changing the ball drop.
Maintain balance throughout the kicking action.
Keep the head over the football.
Finish towards the target.
Explain that longer kicks should feel like a stronger version of the same movement rather than a completely different kick.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether technique changes as distance increases.
Watch for players trying to "muscle" the football instead of accelerating smoothly through the kick.

commonErrors.correction: Keep the chest over the football throughout the kick.

commonErrors.error: Throwing the football onto the boot
commonErrors.correction: Guide the football down naturally from the hands.
Reinforce identical mechanics at every distance.
Slow the approach and finish balanced.
Reduce effort slightly and focus on smooth acceleration.

progressions: Complete the drill using the non-preferred foot.
Introduce target gates at each distance.
regressions: Allow players to repeat each distance until comfortable.
Reduce the number of successful kicks required before progressing.
successIndicators: Maintain correct kicking technique at every distance.
Increase kicking distance without sacrificing balance.
Demonstrate confidence at progressively longer distances.
matchApplication: Footballers constantly adjust the length of their kicks depending on field position and available options. This drill develops the ability to judge kicking weight accurately, allowing players to execute short passes, medium passes and longer field kicks using the same reliable drop punt technique.

title: Non-Preferred Foot Development
objective: Develop confidence and basic competence when kicking with the non-preferred foot. Players practise the same drop punt technique used on their preferred side while working at a shorter distance and lower intensity.
players:
Minimum: 2
Ideal: 10–20
Maximum: Unlimited, working in pairs
setup:
• Players work in pairs facing each other.
• Recommended starting distances:
• Under 8–10: 6–8 metres apart.
• Under 12–14: 8–10 metres apart.
• Under 16 and above: 10–15 metres apart.
• Players begin with the football in the hands they would normally use when kicking on their non-preferred side.
• Spread pairs evenly so inaccurate kicks do not interfere with nearby players.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A performs a stationary drop punt using the non-preferred foot.
2. Player B marks or gathers the football.
3. Player B resets and returns the kick using their non-preferred foot.
4. Players continue at a controlled pace.
5. After several repetitions, players may alternate between preferred and non-preferred feet.
6. If technique breaks down, reduce the distance.
7. Players should not be expected to kick the same distance with both feet immediately.
8. The emphasis is on clean contact, balance and confidence.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Hold the football correctly for the non-preferred side.
Guide the football directly over the non-preferred kicking foot.
Keep the head and chest over the football.
Use a smooth leg swing.
Finish balanced towards the target.
Accept reduced distance while technique develops.
Encourage patience. The non-preferred foot will initially feel less natural.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the football is held over the correct kicking foot.
Whether the player is trying to kick too far.
Provide positive reinforcement for technically sound attempts, even when the kick misses the target.

commonErrors.error: Dropping the football across the body
commonErrors.correction: Hold and guide the football directly over the non-preferred kicking foot.
Reduce the distance and focus on clean contact.
Slow the movement and finish balanced towards the target.

commonErrors.error: Using a short, stabbing leg swing
commonErrors.correction: Encourage a relaxed and complete follow-through.
Use short sets of repeated kicks to build confidence.

progressions: Add a cone gate between players.
Alternate preferred and non-preferred feet every kick.
Introduce a short approach before kicking.
regressions: Allow players to practise the ball drop without kicking.
Use a stationary target rather than a partner.
successIndicators: Guide the football onto the non-preferred foot.
Deliver the football close to the intended target.
Show increased willingness to use the non-preferred side.
matchApplication: Players are often forced onto their non-preferred side by opponents, boundary lines or body position. This drill develops the confidence required to avoid stopping, turning unnecessarily or using a predictable kicking option during a match.

title: Kick and Follow
objective: Teach players to move immediately after disposing of the football rather than remaining stationary. Players kick to a teammate, follow their kick and rotate continuously through the drill.
players:
Minimum: 4
Ideal: 8–16
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
groundSize: Small to Medium Area Approximately 25 m × 15 m per group
setup:
• Create two lines facing each other.
• Place one cone at the front of each line.
• Recommended distance between lines:
• Under 8–10: 10 metres.
• Under 12–14: 15 metres.
• Under 16 and above: 20 metres.
• Place a second cone approximately three metres behind each front cone to organise the waiting players.
• The football begins with the first player in one line.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A kicks to Player B at the opposite line.
2. Player A immediately follows the kick by running to the back of Player B’s line.
3. Player B marks or gathers the football.
4. Player B resets and kicks to the next player in the opposite line.
5. Player B follows the kick to the back of that line.
6. The drill continues in a continuous pattern.
7. Players should communicate the intended target before kicking.
coachingPoints: Prepare the football before reaching the kicking point.
Kick accurately to the receiver’s advantage.
Move immediately after disposal.
Run past the receiver rather than stopping in the middle.
Communicate early.
Maintain appropriate spacing in the lines.
The drill should flow continuously without players standing in the kicking lane.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players move immediately after disposal.
Players crossing through the kicking lane.
If lines become long, create additional groups.

commonErrors.error: Player watches the kick and remains stationary
commonErrors.correction: Run immediately after the football leaves the boot.
Follow the kick outside the main kicking lane.
Demand early voice and eye contact.
Require players to balance before kicking.
Divide players into smaller groups.

progressions: Require players to use the non-preferred foot.
Add a short lead before receiving.
Add a handball before the kick.
regressions: Allow players to walk after kicking.
Remove the follow run until kicking accuracy improves.
Use a stationary partner drill first.
matchApplication: Players must continue working after disposal during a match. Following the football can create: A handball receive. An overlap. Support at the next contest. Defensive cover if possession is lost.

title: Triangle Kicking
objective: Develop the ability to kick accurately at changing angles rather than directly forward. Players learn to adjust their body position, identify the next target and move the football around a triangular pattern.
groundSize: Small to Medium Area Approximately 20 m × 20 m × 20 m
setup:
• Place three cones in a triangle.
• Recommended side lengths:
• Under 8–10: 10–12 metres.
• Under 12–14: 15 metres.
• Under 16 and above: 20 metres.
• Divide players evenly between the three cones.
• The football begins at one cone.
• All kicks initially travel in the same direction around the triangle.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A kicks to Player B at the next cone.
2. Player A follows the kick to the back of Player B’s line.
3. Player B marks or gathers the football.
4. Player B turns, identifies Player C and kicks to the next cone.
5. Player B follows the kick.
6. The pattern continues around the triangle.
7. Change direction after several minutes.
8. Players should turn their body before beginning the kicking action.
coachingPoints: Look towards the next target before receiving.
Mark the football in front of the eyes.
Turn the hips and shoulders towards the target.
Balance before kicking.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage.
Follow the disposal.
Encourage players to avoid catching, stopping completely and then searching for the next target.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players drift inside the triangle.

commonErrors.error: Player receives without knowing the next target
commonErrors.correction: Scan towards the next cone before the football arrives.
Turn the hips and shoulders towards the target first.
Follow the outside edge of the triangle.
Kick slightly in front of the target.

commonErrors.error: Players stop the drill to organise themselves
commonErrors.correction: Use clear cones and demonstrate the rotation before starting.

progressions: Reverse direction on the coach’s call.
Require non-preferred foot kicking on one side.
regressions: Allow players to handball around the triangle first.
Place a coach at each cone to guide the rotation.
successIndicators: Turn towards the correct kicking direction.
Deliver accurate kicks at different angles.
matchApplication: Australian Football rarely requires players to kick in a perfectly straight line. This drill develops the ability to move the football around opponents, change angles and connect with teammates positioned across the ground.

title: Moving Target Kicking
objective: Teach players to kick accurately to a teammate who is moving rather than standing still. Players learn to place the football into the receiver’s running path so they can mark without slowing down or changing direction.
setup:
• Create two lines facing each other approximately 20 metres apart.
• Place a starting cone five metres to the side of each receiving line.
• The first receiver starts at the side cone rather than directly in front of the kicker.
• The football begins with the first player in the opposite line.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The receiver begins at the side cone.
2. The receiver leads diagonally into the space between the two lines.
3. The kicker waits until the receiver begins moving.
4. The kicker delivers the football in front of the receiver.
5. The receiver marks while continuing forward.
6. The receiver carries the football to the opposite line.
7. The kicker moves to the receiving line.
8. The drill repeats in the opposite direction.
9. The lead should begin before the kick is released.
coachingPoints: Communicate before beginning the lead.
Watch the receiver’s movement.
Kick to where the receiver is going.
Place the football slightly in front of the receiver.
Match the weight of the kick to the speed of the lead.
Avoid kicking directly at the receiver’s current position.
The receiver should accelerate into the football rather than waiting underneath it.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Timing between the lead and kick.

commonErrors.correction: Aim further into the receiver’s running path.
Wait until the kicker is balanced and ready.
Kick flatter and further in front.

commonErrors.error: Kicker watches the football instead of the receiver
commonErrors.correction: Scan the receiver before beginning the kicking action.
Require the receiver to call before leading.

progressions: Increase the speed of the lead.
Add a passive defender following the receiver.
regressions: Allow the receiver to walk through the pattern.
Stop and reset after each repetition.
successIndicators: Allow the receiver to maintain speed.
Time the kick with the lead.
Deliver the football at a markable height.
matchApplication: Players regularly kick to teammates who are leading into space. Accurate placement allows the receiver to: Mark without slowing down. Play on quickly. Maintain attacking momentum. Avoid nearby defenders.

title: Lead and Pass
objective: Develop the connection between the kicker and a leading teammate. Players learn when to begin a lead, where to lead and how to deliver the football to the receiver’s advantage.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 9–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create three positions:
• Kicker.
• Leading player.
• Return player.
• Place the kicker and return player approximately 25 metres apart.
• Place the leading player at a starting cone 10–15 metres to the side of the target area.
• Players form lines at each position.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The leading player waits until the kicker has the football and is ready.
2. The leading player accelerates towards the open space.
3. The leading player calls for the football.
4. The kicker delivers the pass in front of the lead.
5. The leading player marks the football.
6. The leading player turns and kicks to the return player.
7. Players rotate:
8. Kicker becomes leader.
9. Leader becomes return player.
10. Return player becomes kicker.
coachingPoints: Delay the lead until the kicker is ready.
Lead decisively rather than jogging.
Communicate early.
Kick to the space in front of the leader.
Avoid kicking over the receiver’s head.
Turn and prepare quickly after marking.
The kicker and leader must work together.
A good lead can still fail if the kick is late, and a good kick can fail if the lead is poorly timed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the leader is forced to stop.

commonErrors.error: Leader starts before the kicker is ready
commonErrors.correction: Wait until the kicker has control and eye contact.
Accelerate strongly into the available space.

commonErrors.error: Kick goes directly at the player
commonErrors.correction: Aim one to three metres in front of the lead.
Begin the kicking action as soon as the lead is recognised.
Demonstrate the three-position rotation before starting.

progressions: Allow the leader to choose between two directions.
Require a quick play-on after the mark.
Use the non-preferred foot when the lead goes to one side.
regressions: Allow the leader to walk through the pattern.
successIndicators: Deliver the football in front of the receiver.
matchApplication: This drill replicates the basic connection between a ball carrier and a teammate leading into space. It applies to: Forward leads. Wing outlets. Defensive exits. Centre corridor movement. Short possession kicks.

title: Continuous Kicking Circuit
objective: Combine accurate kicking, marking and movement in a continuous drill. Players learn to prepare quickly, dispose of the football and move immediately to the next position.
setup:
• Place four cones in a square or diamond.
• Recommended spacing:
• Under 10: 12–15 metres.
• Under 12–14: 15–20 metres.
• Under 16 and above: 20–25 metres.
• Divide players evenly between the four cones.
• Place one football at two opposite cones.
• All footballs initially travel in the same direction.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The first players at the two starting cones kick simultaneously to the next cone.
2. Each kicker follows the football to the back of the receiving line.
3. The receivers mark or gather the football.
4. They turn, identify the next target and kick to the following cone.
5. The footballs continue around the circuit.
6. Players follow every kick.
7. Change direction after several minutes.
8. Players must remain aware of both footballs and avoid entering another player’s kicking lane.
coachingPoints: Prepare before receiving.
Scan towards the next target.
Communicate early.
Kick accurately.
Follow every disposal.
Stay outside the central area.
Maintain appropriate spacing between footballs.
Accuracy should be maintained before speed is increased.

commonErrors.error: Players watch their kick instead of moving
commonErrors.correction: Follow the football immediately after disposal.
Follow the outside edge of the circuit.
Delay one starting group or increase spacing.

commonErrors.error: Receiver is surprised by the kick
commonErrors.correction: Require early voice and eye contact.
Reduce tempo and restore accurate execution.

progressions: Reverse direction on the coach’s call.
Require non-preferred foot kicking on selected sides.
Add a moving lead at each cone.
Add a handball receive before each kick.
regressions: Walk through the circuit before increasing pace.
Pause after each kick until players understand the rotation.
successIndicators: Keep the circuit moving without unnecessary stoppages.
matchApplication: Australian Football requires players to make repeated decisions and execute skills without standing still. This drill develops the ability to: Move after disposal. Connect multiple possessions. Scan before receiving. Maintain skill execution during continuous movement.

title: Kicking to Multiple Leads
objective: Develop the kicker’s ability to identify and select between multiple leading targets. Players learn to scan before receiving, recognise the best available option and deliver the football to the selected receiver’s advantage.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 9–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create one kicking position and two leading lanes.
• Place the kicker approximately 25 metres from the target area.
• Set two starting cones approximately 10 metres apart for the leading players.
• Place a waiting line behind each leading cone.
• A feeder stands five to ten metres behind the kicker with the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder passes the football to the kicker.
2. As the kicker receives the football, the first player from each leading line begins a lead.
3. One player leads left and the other leads right.
4. The kicker scans both options and selects one target.
5. The kicker delivers the football to the selected player’s advantage.
6. The selected receiver marks the football and returns it to the feeder.
7. The unselected player completes the lead before returning to the back of their line.
8. The kicker rotates into one of the leading lines.
9. A new kicker moves into position.
10. Continue for the allocated time.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan before receiving the football.
Keep both leading options within vision.
Select the player with the greatest space.
Make the decision early.
Kick to where the receiver is moving.
Avoid staring at the selected target too early.
Deliver the football at a markable height.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the kicker scans before receiving.
Whether the kicker consistently favours one side.
Whether unselected players complete their leads.

commonErrors.correction: Scan both leading lanes before receiving the football.
Select the option as the leads begin rather than after they finish.
Place the football further into the receiver’s running path.

commonErrors.error: Both leaders move into the same space
commonErrors.correction: Allocate separate leading lanes.

commonErrors.error: Kicker always chooses the preferred side
commonErrors.correction: Encourage selection based on space rather than kicking-foot preference.

progressions: Add a passive defender between the leading players.
Allow leading players to choose their own direction.
Require non-preferred foot use when selecting one side.
regressions: Use one leading option at a time.
Tell the kicker which option to select.
Allow the kicker to begin with the football.
successIndicators: Select the player in the greatest space.
Make decisions before the lead is completed.
Deliver the football to the receiver’s advantage.
matchApplication: Ball carriers regularly have several teammates presenting at the same time. This drill develops the ability to identify the best option rather than automatically kicking to the first player seen or the loudest voice.

title: Lead Direction Decision
objective: Teach players to recognise and respond to a receiver who can lead in more than one direction. The kicker must delay the decision until the receiver commits to a lead and then place the football into the correct space.
players:
Minimum: 5
Ideal: 8–16
Maximum: 20 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place one kicking cone approximately 25 metres from the leading area.
• Place one starting cone for the receiver directly ahead of the kicker.
• Place two target cones approximately eight metres apart, one to the left and one to the right of the receiver’s starting position.
• Players form one line at the kicking cone and one line at the receiver’s starting cone.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The first kicker begins with the football.
2. The receiver starts facing the kicker.
3. On the coach’s call, the receiver chooses to lead towards either the left or right target cone.
4. The kicker reads the direction of the lead.
5. The kicker delivers the football into the receiver’s path.
6. The receiver marks or gathers the football.
7. The receiver returns the football to the kicking line.
8. The kicker moves to the receiver’s line.
9. The receiver returns to the back of the kicking line.
10. Continue for the allocated time.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Keep the receiver within vision.
Avoid deciding before the receiver moves.
Read the receiver’s first committed steps.
Turn the hips and shoulders towards the selected target.
Kick into the space ahead of the receiver.
Use controlled kicking weight.
The kicker should remain balanced while waiting for the lead to develop.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the kicker guesses the direction.
Reaction time after the lead begins.
Whether players remain balanced while waiting.
Encourage the kicker to react calmly rather than rush.

commonErrors.error: Kicker guesses before the receiver moves
commonErrors.correction: Keep the body neutral until the lead direction is clear.

commonErrors.error: Kick goes across the player’s path
commonErrors.correction: Turn the hips and shoulders towards the selected side.
Require one decisive lead.
Begin the kicking action after the receiver’s first committed steps.
Stay balanced with light movement while waiting.

progressions: Increase the speed of the lead.
Allow the receiver to lead forward, left or right.
Require the kicker to receive a handball before making the decision.
regressions: Tell the kicker the lead direction before the repetition.
Reduce the distance between kicker and receiver.
Slow the receiver to walking pace.
Use only one direction for several repetitions.
Allow the kicker additional preparation time.
successIndicators: Wait until the lead direction is clear.
Align the body with the selected target.
Deliver the football at a markable height.
matchApplication: Receivers frequently change their leading direction based on space, defenders and ball-carrier position. This drill develops the patience and awareness required to read the lead rather than forcing the receiver towards a predetermined location.

title: Kick to Space
objective: Develop the ability to kick the football into open space rather than directly at a teammate. Players learn to recognise where the receiver can move next and place the football in a location that maintains attacking momentum.
players:
Minimum: 5
Ideal: 8–16
Maximum: 20 using multiple groups
equipment: Optional flat markers for target zones.
setup:
• Create one kicking cone and three target zones.
• Place the target zones approximately 20–30 metres from the kicker:
• One directly ahead.
• One to the left.
• One to the right.
• Each target zone should be approximately four metres wide and six metres long.
• A receiver begins approximately five metres behind the target zones.
• Players form lines at the kicking and receiving positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The kicker begins with the football.
2. The receiver moves forward and selects one of the three target zones.
3. The kicker identifies the receiver’s movement.
4. The kicker places the football into the selected target zone.
5. The receiver marks or gathers the football while continuing through the zone.
6. The receiver returns the football to the kicking line.
7. Players rotate positions.
8. Continue for the allocated time.
9. The receiver should not stop inside the zone and wait for the football.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Identify open space before kicking.
Place the football ahead of the receiver.
Use appropriate kicking weight.
Keep the kick away from imaginary defensive pressure.
Select a flatter kick when the receiver is moving quickly.
Avoid forcing the receiver to stop or move backwards.
Explain that the target is the space, not the player’s current body position.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the kicker watches the receiver.
Whether players kick directly at the receiver.
Praise well-placed kicks even when the receiver does not mark cleanly.

commonErrors.error: Kick travels directly to the receiver
commonErrors.correction: Aim for the open space ahead of the lead.

commonErrors.error: Kick carries beyond the target zone
commonErrors.correction: Reduce kicking power and improve touch.

commonErrors.error: Receiver stops before the football arrives
commonErrors.correction: Require the receiver to continue moving through the zone.
Use a flatter trajectory to maintain momentum.

commonErrors.error: Kicker waits until the receiver reaches the zone
commonErrors.correction: Release the kick earlier.

progressions: Reduce the size of the target zones.
Allow the receiver to change direction.
Require non-preferred foot kicking to selected zones.
regressions: Tell the receiver which zone to use.
Slow the receiver to jogging pace.
Allow the kicker to begin closer to the target.
successIndicators: Place the football ahead of the receiver.
Allow the receiver to maintain speed.
Avoid kicking directly at the player.
matchApplication: Effective teams often kick to space rather than to stationary teammates. This skill is used during: Forward entries. Wing transitions. Defensive exits. Fast breaks. Kicks over or around defensive pressure.

title: Short Approach Drop Punt
primarySkill: Drop Punt from a Short Approach
objective: Progress players from stationary kicking to executing a drop punt after a short, controlled approach. Players learn to coordinate their steps, ball preparation and kicking action without rushing.
players:
Minimum: 2
Ideal: 8–20
Maximum: Unlimited, working in pairs
groundSize: Small to Medium Area Approximately 25 m × 20 m
setup:
• Players work in pairs facing each other.
• Place a starting cone approximately three metres behind each player’s kicking cone.
• Recommended kicking distances:
• Under 8–10: 8–10 metres.
• Under 12–14: 12–15 metres.
• Under 16 and above: 15–20 metres.
• Players begin at the rear starting cone.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A begins with the football at the starting cone.
2. Player A walks or jogs forward for two to four controlled steps.
3. Player A performs a drop punt from the kicking cone.
4. Player B marks or gathers the football.
5. Player B resets at their starting cone.
6. Player B repeats the short approach and kick.
7. Continue for the allocated time.
8. Increase approach speed only when technique remains consistent.
9. The approach should remain controlled rather than becoming a sprint.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Prepare the football during the approach.
Keep the final steps controlled.
Maintain balance before contact.
Guide the football onto the boot.
Avoid taking an excessively long final step.
Follow through towards the target.
Continue moving naturally after the kick.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player rushes as speed increases.

commonErrors.correction: Slow the approach and regain control.
Position the football before the final two steps.
Shorten the final step to keep the body balanced.
Maintain smooth forward momentum through the kick.

commonErrors.error: Ball drop moves across the body
commonErrors.correction: Guide the football directly over the kicking foot.

progressions: Progress to a continuous running kick.
Receive a handball before beginning the approach.
regressions: Allow players to rehearse the steps without the football.
successIndicators: Coordinate the approach and kicking action.
matchApplication: Players rarely kick from a completely stationary position during general play. This drill introduces the movement coordination required to prepare and execute the football while approaching the point of disposal.

title: Running Drop Punt
objective: Develop the ability to execute an accurate drop punt while running at controlled speed. Players learn to prepare the football early, manage their final steps and maintain forward momentum through the kick.
players:
Minimum: 4
Ideal: 8–16
Maximum: 20 using multiple lanes
groundSize: Medium Area Approximately 35 m × 20 m per lane
setup:
• Create a straight kicking lane.
• Place:
• A starting cone.
• A kicking cone 10 metres ahead.
• A receiving cone 15–25 metres beyond the kicking cone.
• Players form lines at the starting and receiving cones.
• The football begins with the first player at the starting cone.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A runs from the starting cone while carrying the football.
2. Player A prepares the football before reaching the kicking cone.
3. Player A executes a drop punt while continuing forward.
4. Player B marks or gathers the football at the receiving cone.
5. Player A continues running to the back of the receiving line.
6. Player B carries the football to the opposite starting position or returns the kick through a second lane.
7. Continue for the allocated time.
8. Players should begin at controlled pace before progressing towards game speed.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Carry the football securely.
Prepare the ball before the final steps.
Keep the final stride controlled.
Maintain the head over the football.
Kick through the target.
Continue running after disposal.
Avoid jumping or leaning backwards.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players slow excessively or rush.

commonErrors.error: Ball is prepared at the last moment
commonErrors.correction: Move the football into kicking position earlier.

commonErrors.error: Player takes an excessively long final step
commonErrors.correction: Shorten and control the final stride.
Keep the support foot closer to the ground and remain balanced.
Reduce running speed until technique improves.
Continue running towards the receiving position.

successIndicators: Execute without significantly slowing before the kick.
matchApplication: Running drop punts are used throughout general play when players: Break from congestion. Carry the football through space. Deliver inside 50. Exit defence. Complete an overlap. Attack through the corridor.

title: Receive, Run and Kick
objective: Develop the ability to receive the football, move quickly into space and execute an accurate kick. Players learn to prepare the next action before taking possession and avoid unnecessary delays after the mark or gather.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 9–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create three stations in a straight or slightly angled line:
• Feeder.
• Receiver.
• Final target.
• Place the feeder and receiver approximately 15 metres apart.
• Place the final target approximately 20 metres beyond the receiver.
• Players form lines at all three stations.
• The football begins with the feeder.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder kicks to the receiver.
2. Before the football arrives, the receiver scans towards the final target.
3. The receiver marks or gathers the football.
4. The receiver immediately runs forward for five to ten metres.
5. The receiver delivers a running drop punt to the final target.
6. The final target marks the football.
7. Players rotate:
8. Feeder becomes receiver.
9. Receiver becomes final target.
10. Final target returns to the feeder line.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan before receiving.
Mark the football in front of the eyes.
Move immediately after possession.
Carry the football securely.
Prepare the ball early.
Balance through the running kick.
Deliver the football to the final target’s advantage.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the receiver scans before possession.
Speed of movement after the mark.

commonErrors.error: Receiver watches only the incoming football
commonErrors.correction: Scan towards the next target before the mark.
Move immediately into the open space.
Position the football during the run rather than at the kicking cone.
Control the final steps and maintain balance.

commonErrors.error: Final target remains stationary and silent
commonErrors.correction: Require early communication and visible hands.

progressions: Require a bounce during the run.
regressions: Allow the receiver to walk after marking.
Remove the initial kick and begin with a handball.
Pause after the mark before beginning the run.
matchApplication: Players often receive possession and must immediately carry the football before delivering to the next teammate. This drill applies to: Half-back rebound. Wing transition. Centre-square exits. Overlap running. Forward entries. Switching play.

title: Running Kick Through Gates
objective: Develop accurate kicking while running by requiring players to execute a drop punt through a target gate. Players learn to control their final steps, align their body and maintain accuracy without stopping before disposal.
players:
Minimum: 4
Ideal: 8–16
Maximum: 20 using multiple lanes
groundSize: Medium Area Approximately 35 m × 15 m per lane
setup:
• Create a straight running lane.
• Place:
• A starting cone.
• A kicking cone approximately 10 metres ahead.
• A two-metre-wide target gate approximately 10 metres beyond the kicking cone.
• A receiving cone five to ten metres beyond the gate.
• Players form lines at the starting and receiving cones.
• The football begins at the starting line.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A runs from the starting cone with the football.
2. Player A prepares the football before reaching the kicking cone.
3. Player A performs a running drop punt through the target gate.
4. Player B marks or gathers the football beyond the gate.
5. Player A continues to the back of Player B’s line.
6. Player B returns through the opposite lane or carries the football to the starting line.
7. Continue for the allocated time.
8. Reverse the lane direction so players practise kicking from both sides.
9. Players score one point each time the football travels cleanly through the gate.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Prepare the football before the final steps.
Keep the hips and shoulders aligned with the gate.
Control the final stride.
Guide the football directly onto the kicking foot.
Continue running through the kick.
Finish with the kicking leg pointing towards the target.
Accuracy should remain the priority as running speed increases.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the football passes through the gate.
Whether players slow excessively before kicking.
Reduce speed or widen the gate if technique begins to deteriorate.

commonErrors.error: Player prepares the football too late
commonErrors.correction: Move the football into kicking position before reaching the kicking cone.
Align the hips and shoulders with the gate.
Maintain controlled forward momentum through disposal.
Shorten the final step to improve balance.
Reduce running pace until accuracy improves.

progressions: Introduce a moving receiver beyond the gate.
regressions: Allow players to jog rather than run.
matchApplication: Players often carry the football through space before kicking between opponents or into a narrow passing lane. This drill develops the accuracy required to complete those kicks without losing attacking speed.

title: Bounce and Kick
objective: Develop the ability to complete a controlled running bounce before preparing and executing an accurate drop punt. Players learn to regain possession cleanly and transition smoothly from running to kicking.
players:
Minimum: 4
Ideal: 8–16
Maximum: 20 using multiple lanes
groundSize: Medium Area Approximately 40 m × 15 m per lane
setup:
• Create a straight lane.
• Place:
• A starting cone.
• A bounce cone approximately 10 metres ahead.
• A kicking cone another eight to ten metres ahead.
• A receiving cone 15–25 metres beyond the kicking cone.
• Players form lines at the starting and receiving cones.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A runs from the starting cone carrying the football.
2. Player A completes one running bounce near the bounce cone.
3. Player A regathers the football cleanly.
4. Player A prepares the football before reaching the kicking cone.
5. Player A performs a running drop punt to Player B.
6. Player B marks or gathers the football.
7. Player A continues to the receiving line.
8. Player B returns through the opposite lane or carries the football back to the start.
9. Continue for the allocated time.
10. The bounce should be completed early enough to allow time for controlled ball preparation.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Bounce the football in front of the body.
Keep the bounce low and controlled.
Regather with two hands.
Secure possession before preparing to kick.
Avoid rushing immediately after the bounce.
Control the final steps.
Maintain accuracy to the receiver.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players look down for too long.

commonErrors.error: Bounce is too close to the body
commonErrors.correction: Push the football slightly forward into the running path.
Use a firmer, lower bounce.

commonErrors.error: Player attempts to kick immediately after regathering
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and prepare the football before kicking.

commonErrors.error: Player looks down for the entire run
commonErrors.correction: Glance at the bounce, then lift the eyes towards the target.

commonErrors.error: Bounce occurs too close to the kicking cone
commonErrors.correction: Complete the bounce earlier in the lane.

progressions: Require the player to choose between kicking targets.
regressions: Reduce the distance of the run.
Allow players to bounce and stop before kicking.
matchApplication: Players frequently need to bounce while carrying the football before disposing. This drill develops the coordination required to maintain speed, meet the running-bounce requirement and execute the next kick accurately.

title: Handball Receive and Kick
objective: Develop the ability to receive a handball while moving and quickly transition into an accurate kick. Players learn to time their support run, receive cleanly and prepare the football without breaking stride.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 9–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create three positions:
• Ball carrier.
• Support runner.
• Kicking target.
• Place the support runner’s starting cone approximately five metres beside and behind the ball carrier.
• Place the kicking target 20–30 metres ahead.
• Players form lines at all three positions.
• The football begins with the ball carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The ball carrier begins jogging forward.
2. The support runner accelerates alongside and calls for the football.
3. The ball carrier handballs into the support runner’s path.
4. The support runner receives without stopping.
5. The support runner carries the football for several steps.
6. The support runner kicks to the final target.
7. Players rotate:
8. Ball carrier becomes support runner.
9. Support runner becomes final target.
10. Final target returns to the ball-carrier line.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Time the support run.
Communicate before receiving.
Present hands clearly.
Receive the football in front of the body.
Move the football into kicking position early.
Control the final steps.
Kick to the final target’s advantage.

commonErrors.correction: Delay the run until the ball carrier begins moving.
Place the football in front of the runner.
Secure the football before preparing to kick.

commonErrors.error: Player takes too many steps before kicking
commonErrors.correction: Prepare the football earlier.
Accelerate through the receiving point.

progressions: Require the receiver to use the non-preferred foot.
Begin with a ground ball gather.
Add a second handball before the kick.
regressions: Allow players to stop after receiving.
Remove the final target and kick through a wide gate.
matchApplication: This drill replicates an overlap or release handball where the receiving player becomes the next kicker. It applies to: Half-back rebound. Midfield overlap. Corridor attack. Forward entries. Exiting congestion.

title: Turn and Kick
objective: Develop the ability to receive the football facing away from the intended target, turn efficiently and execute an accurate kick. Players learn to scan before possession and reposition the body without losing balance.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 9–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create three positions in a straight line:
• Feeder.
• Receiver.
• Final target.
• The receiver begins with their back or side facing the final target.
• Place the feeder approximately 10–15 metres from the receiver.
• Place the final target approximately 20 metres beyond the receiver.
• Players form lines at each position.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The receiver scans over the shoulder towards the final target.
2. The feeder kicks or handballs to the receiver.
3. The receiver marks or gathers the football.
4. The receiver turns towards the final target.
5. The receiver balances and delivers an accurate kick.
6. The final target marks the football.
7. Players rotate through each position.
8. Change the turning direction after several repetitions.
9. Players should scan before the football arrives rather than waiting until after possession.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan before receiving.
Mark or gather securely.
Turn using short, controlled steps.
Keep the football protected.
Align the hips and shoulders with the target.
Balance before kicking.
Avoid swinging across the body.

commonErrors.error: Receiver does not scan before possession
commonErrors.correction: Check over the shoulder before the football arrives.

commonErrors.error: Player takes too many steps to turn
commonErrors.correction: Use shorter and quicker footwork.

commonErrors.error: Football is exposed during the turn
commonErrors.correction: Hold the football securely and close to the body.
Complete the turn and square the hips first.
Balance after turning before beginning the disposal.

progressions: Allow the final target to move.
Require a turn onto the non-preferred side.
Receive a ground ball instead of a pass.
Reduce the time allowed to dispose.
regressions: Tell players which direction to turn.
Allow the receiver to stop after turning.
successIndicators: Deliver accurate kicks in both directions.
matchApplication: Players frequently receive the football while facing away from goal or the next target. This skill applies to: Marks on the boundary. Ground balls in congestion. Defensive switches. Midfield possessions. Forward entries after turning from pressure.
relatedDrills: KK-022 – Ground Ball Gather and Kick

title: Change of Direction Kick
objective: Develop the ability to change running direction before executing an accurate kick. Players learn to regain balance after cutting, prepare the football early and align their body with a new target.
players:
Minimum: 4
Ideal: 8–16
Maximum: 20 using multiple lanes
setup:
• Create a zigzag running lane.
• Place:
• A starting cone.
• A direction-change cone five to eight metres ahead and to one side.
• A second direction-change cone five to eight metres ahead on the opposite side.
• A kicking cone beyond the second turn.
• A receiving cone 15–25 metres ahead.
• Players form lines at the starting and receiving positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A runs from the starting cone with the football.
2. Player A changes direction around the first cone.
3. Player A changes direction again around the second cone.
4. Player A prepares the football before reaching the kicking cone.
5. Player A performs a running drop punt to Player B.
6. Player B marks or gathers the football.
7. Player A continues to the receiving line.
8. Player B returns through an opposite lane or carries the football back.
9. Change the cone pattern after several minutes.
10. Players should maintain control through each direction change.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Lower the body before changing direction.
Use short steps through the turn.
Keep the football secure.
Regain balance before kicking.
Align the body with the final target.
Prepare the football before the kicking cone.
Avoid rushing after the final turn.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players drift outside the lane.

commonErrors.error: Player remains upright through the turn
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips and bend the knees.

commonErrors.error: Football moves loosely during direction changes
commonErrors.correction: Secure it with two hands when changing direction.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks while still off balance
commonErrors.correction: Regain control before beginning the kicking action.
Align the hips and shoulders with the target.
Use shorter steps closer to each cone.

progressions: Add a bounce before the first turn.
Allow the coach to call the direction of the first turn.
regressions: Allow players to stop before kicking.
successIndicators: Complete the movement without unnecessary stopping.
matchApplication: Players often need to evade pressure, change direction and then dispose of the football. This skill is used when: Escaping congestion. Moving around an opponent. Changing the angle of attack. Creating space before a forward entry. Rebounding from defence.
relatedDrills: KK-022 – Ground Ball Gather and Kick

title: Ground Ball Gather and Kick
primarySkill: Kicking After a Ground Ball Gather
objective: Develop the ability to collect a ground ball cleanly, accelerate away from the contest and execute an accurate kick. Players learn to secure possession before transitioning quickly into the kicking action.
players:
Minimum: 4
Ideal: 8–16
Maximum: 20 using multiple lanes
setup:
• Create a straight lane.
• Place:
• A starting cone.
• A ground-ball cone five to eight metres ahead.
• A kicking cone another five to eight metres ahead.
• A receiving cone 15–25 metres beyond the kicking cone.
• A feeder stands beside the ground-ball cone.
• Players form lines at the starting and receiving cones.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A runs from the starting cone.
2. The feeder rolls the football into Player A’s path.
3. Player A lowers the body and gathers the football cleanly.
4. Player A accelerates away from the collection point.
5. Player A prepares the football before reaching the kicking cone.
6. Player A executes a running drop punt to Player B.
7. Player B marks or gathers the football.
8. Player A continues to the receiving line.
9. Player B returns to the starting line with the football.
10. Rotate the feeder regularly.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Approach the football with controlled speed.
Lower the hips and keep the head over the ball.
Use two hands whenever possible.
Gather the football cleanly before accelerating.
Take the first steps away from the collection point.
Prepare the football early.
Balance through the running kick.

commonErrors.error: Player bends only at the waist
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips and bend the knees.
Gather with two hands whenever space allows.

commonErrors.error: Player looks towards the target before securing the football
commonErrors.correction: Complete the collection before lifting the eyes.
Accelerate first, then move the football into kicking position.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks while leaning forward excessively
commonErrors.correction: Regain balance during the steps after the gather.

progressions: Increase the speed or angle of the ground ball.
Require the player to change direction after gathering.
Begin with a contested ground ball.
regressions: Allow the player to stop after gathering.
Remove the kicking component until collection improves.
successIndicators: Complete the sequence without unnecessary delay.
matchApplication: Ground balls regularly begin attacking possessions. Players must collect cleanly, escape immediate pressure and deliver accurately to a teammate. This drill applies to: Loose-ball wins. Crumbing. Contested-ball exits. Defensive rebounds. Midfield stoppage releases.

title: Overlap Run and Kick
objective: Develop the ability to create an overlap, receive a handball at speed and deliver an accurate kick. Players learn to time their supporting run so they receive the football in front of the original ball carrier and continue the attacking movement.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 9–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create three positions:
• Initial ball carrier.
• Overlap runner.
• Final kicking target.
• Place the overlap runner approximately five metres behind and to the side of the initial ball carrier.
• Place the final target 25–35 metres ahead.
• Players form lines at all three positions.
• The football begins with the initial ball carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The initial ball carrier begins moving forward.
2. The overlap runner delays briefly before accelerating past on the outside.
3. The overlap runner calls for the football.
4. The initial ball carrier handballs into the runner’s path.
5. The overlap runner receives without slowing.
6. The overlap runner carries the football for several steps.
7. The overlap runner kicks to the final target.
8. Players rotate:
9. Initial ball carrier becomes overlap runner.
10. Overlap runner becomes final target.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Delay the support run until the ball carrier begins moving.
Accelerate past at the correct angle.
Communicate early.
Receive the handball in front of the body.
Prepare the football while maintaining speed.
Control the final steps.
Deliver the kick to the target’s advantage.

commonErrors.correction: Delay until the ball carrier begins moving.

commonErrors.error: Runner receives beside or behind the ball carrier
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate past before calling for the handball.
Place the football into the runner’s forward path.
Prepare the football earlier and maintain momentum.
Widen the overlap angle.

progressions: Require non-preferred foot kicking from one side.
Allow the ball carrier to decide whether to handball or retain possession.
regressions: Allow the receiver to stop before kicking.
Walk through the running pattern before increasing speed.
successIndicators: Receive in front of the ball carrier.
matchApplication: Overlap running is used to: Break defensive lines. Create an extra player in attack. Move the football from half-back. Generate forward momentum. Deliver inside 50 with reduced pressure.

title: Evasion and Kick
objective: Develop the ability to evade an opponent or obstacle before executing an accurate kick. Players learn to change direction under control, protect the football and regain balance before disposal.
players:
Minimum: 5
Ideal: 8–16
Maximum: 20 using multiple lanes
equipment: Optional agility pole or passive defender.
setup:
• Create one running lane.
• Place:
• A starting cone.
• An evasion point approximately eight metres ahead.
• Two exit gates, one left and one right of the evasion point.
• A kicking cone beyond each exit gate.
• A receiving target 20–30 metres ahead.
• A coach or passive defender stands at the evasion point.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A runs towards the evasion point with the football.
2. The coach or passive defender moves slightly towards one side.
3. Player A changes direction through the opposite exit gate.
4. Player A secures the football and regains balance.
5. Player A executes a running drop punt to Player B.
6. Player B marks or gathers the football.
7. Player A continues to the receiving line.
8. Player B returns to the starting line.
9. Change the defender’s movement regularly.
10. The defender provides visual pressure without tackling.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Approach under control.
Keep the football secure during the evasive movement.
Read the defender’s position.
Change direction with short steps.
Accelerate through the exit gate.
Regain balance before kicking.
Align with the target after the evasion.

commonErrors.correction: Read the defender before selecting the exit gate.
Secure the football with two hands through the evasion.

commonErrors.error: Player makes a wide, slow turn
commonErrors.correction: Use shorter steps and stay closer to the evasion point.

commonErrors.error: Kick is rushed immediately after the move
commonErrors.correction: Take controlled steps to regain balance.

commonErrors.error: Player continues drifting sideways while kicking
commonErrors.correction: Straighten towards the target before disposal.

progressions: Reduce the width of the exit gates.
Require the non-preferred foot after one exit.
Allow the player to use a sidestep, baulk or change of pace.
regressions: Replace the defender with a stationary pole.
Tell the player which gate to use.
Allow the player to stop before kicking.
matchApplication: Players often need to create kicking space by: Sidestepping an opponent. Changing direction. Moving around a mark. Escaping congestion. Avoiding frontal pressure.
relatedDrills: KK-022 – Ground Ball Gather and Kick

title: Contested Gather and Kick
objective: Develop the ability to win or secure a contested ground ball, escape pressure and execute an effective kick. Players learn to place the body between the opponent and the football before creating enough space to dispose accurately.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 10–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create:
• A feeder position.
• A contest area approximately six metres wide.
• Two exit gates beyond the contest.
• One kicking target 20–30 metres ahead.
• Two players begin on opposite sides of the contest area.
• The feeder stands five to ten metres away with the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder rolls or bounces the football into the contest area.
2. Both players compete to gain possession.
3. The player who wins the football protects it and exits through either gate.
4. The opposing player applies controlled pressure without completing a full tackle.
5. The ball winner accelerates into space.
6. The ball winner kicks to the target.
7. Players reset and rotate.
8. Alternate opponents regularly.
9. The drill ends if the football becomes trapped for an extended period. Restart with a new feed.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Approach the football with the body low.
Keep the feet moving.
Position the body between the opponent and the football.
Gather with two hands when possible.
Protect possession.
Exit away from pressure.
Lift the eyes after escaping.

commonErrors.error: Player reaches without using the body
commonErrors.correction: Win position between the opponent and football first.

commonErrors.error: Player stands upright at the contest
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips and keep the feet moving.

commonErrors.error: Ball winner tries to kick immediately
commonErrors.correction: Exit pressure before preparing the disposal.

commonErrors.error: Player runs directly into the opponent
commonErrors.correction: Use the open gate away from pressure.
Regain balance after the exit before kicking.

progressions: Require a handball receive before kicking.
Reduce the size of the exit gates.
Allow full tackling for appropriately prepared groups.
regressions: Roll the football directly towards one player.
Allow the ball winner to stop after exiting.
successIndicators: Recover quickly after losing the contest.
matchApplication: This drill replicates possessions that begin with: A loose ball. A stoppage spill. A marking contest. A defensive ground ball. A forward-half turnover. Players must secure possession before creating a usable disposal.
relatedDrills: KK-022 – Ground Ball Gather and Kick

title: Two-on-One Release Kick
objective: Develop the ability to use a two-on-one advantage to release one player into space for an effective kick. Players learn to draw the defender, support at the correct angle and identify when the kicker has been freed.
players:
Minimum: 7
Ideal: 10–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create a channel approximately 15 metres wide and 25 metres long.
• Place:
• Two attacking starting cones at one end.
• One defender in the middle of the channel.
• One final kicking target 20 metres beyond the channel.
• The two attackers begin side by side, with one holding the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The two attackers move into the channel.
2. The defender applies pressure and attempts to stop forward movement.
3. The ball carrier decides whether to:
4. Carry the football and draw the defender.
5. Handball to the support runner.
6. The attackers use the two-on-one advantage to release one player beyond the defender.
7. The released player kicks to the final target.
8. Players rotate through attacking, defending and target roles.
9. Continue for the allocated time.
10. The defender uses passive or controlled pressure according to the age and experience of the group.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Maintain width between attackers.
Run forward rather than sideways.
Draw the defender before releasing the football.
Support at an angle that allows continued movement.
Communicate clearly.
Receive in space.
Prepare quickly for the final kick.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the released player remains free.

commonErrors.correction: Maintain width so the defender cannot cover both players.
Carry closer and draw the defender first.
Accelerate past into an attacking position.
Use only the disposal required to free the kicker.
Use the space created to balance before disposal.

progressions: Require the final kick to a moving target.

2. The attacker accelerates towards the kicking line.
3. The defender chases and applies pressure without tackling.

5. The attacker kicks to the target before the defender closes.

7. Players rotate roles.
8. Adjust the defender’s starting distance to create appropriate pressure.

Accelerate immediately.
Keep the football secure.
Scan the target early.
Prepare the football before pressure arrives.
Avoid looking backwards repeatedly.
Control the final steps.
Complete the kick rather than simply disposing quickly.

Move the football into position earlier.
Control the final steps before disposal.

Add a second defender approaching from the side.

title: Closing Defender Kick

Ideal: 10–18

howTheDrillWorks:
1. On the coach’s signal, the attacker moves forward.
2. The defender closes from the front with hands raised to create smothering pressure.
3. The attacker identifies the clearer target gate.
4. The attacker adjusts slightly left or right to create a kicking lane.
5. The attacker delivers the football through the chosen gate.
6. The defender avoids contact with the kicking leg.
7. Players rotate through attacking, defending and receiving roles.
8. Continue for the allocated time.
9. The defender’s role is to reduce time and space without tackling.

Scan both targets early.
Recognise the defender’s line.
Move slightly off the line of pressure.
Prepare the football before the defender arrives.
Keep the kick compact and controlled.
Avoid kicking directly into the defender.
Remain composed.

Whether the attacker panics or retreats.

title: Defender Decision Kick

5. The kicker delivers the football to the chosen receiver.

Scan all options before receiving.
Identify the defender’s position.
Avoid kicking towards the option under greatest pressure.
Make the decision early.

Remain composed rather than rushing.

2. The defender closes and raises the hands to threaten a smother.

5. Moving slightly left or right.

Recognise the smothering line.

Use small lateral movements.

Prepare early.
Remain balanced.
Complete the kick only when the lane is clear.

Scan before receiving.
Know the available targets.
Prepare the football immediately.
Take only the steps required.
Remain calm under the countdown.

Maintain technical quality.

Maintain a strong running line.
Use the body to protect possession.
Avoid leaning excessively into the defender.
Regain balance before the final step.
Align the kick with the target.
Continue moving after disposal.

Maintain the head over the ball.
