5. The kicker resets the body.
6. The kicker delivers to the opposite target.
7. Players rotate through each role.
8. Vary the direction of the fake.
9. The fake should be controlled and believable.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan both targets before the fake.
Use the eyes and shoulders to sell the first option.
Keep the football secure.
Avoid overcommitting the body.
Regain balance quickly.
Align with the real target.
Complete the kick with normal technique.

commonErrors.error: Fake is too small to move the defender
commonErrors.correction: Use clearer eyes and shoulder movement.
Keep the feet controlled and the body centred.

commonErrors.error: Football is moved loosely during the fake
commonErrors.correction: Hold it securely until the real kicking action begins.
Improve the timing and realism of the first option.
Reset the body before disposal.

progressions: Allow the defender to choose whether to react.
regressions: Use a coach as the defender.
Allow the kicker to begin with the football.
successIndicators: Move the defender with the fake.
matchApplication: Fakes are used to: Move a player on the mark. Open a corridor kick. Create a switch option. Avoid a smother. Disguise a forward entry. Create time in congestion.
relatedDrills: KK-039 – Short Mark and Switch Kick
KK-041 – Switch Kick to Moving Target

title: Switch Kick to Moving Target
primarySkill: Switching Play to a Moving Receiver
objective: Develop the ability to recognise a switch opportunity and deliver accurately to a teammate moving into open space on the opposite side of the ground. Players learn to scan early, open the body and weight the kick so the receiver can maintain momentum.
players:
Minimum: 7
Ideal: 10–18
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
groundSize: Medium to Large Area Approximately 45 m × 35 m
setup:
• Create three main positions:
• Initial feeder.
• Central receiver.
• Switch receiver.
• Place the feeder and central receiver approximately 15 metres apart.
• Position the switch receiver’s starting cone 20–30 metres away on the opposite side and slightly forward of the central player.
• Place a target cone another five to ten metres ahead of the switch receiver’s starting position.
• Players form lines at each position.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The central player scans towards the switch side.
2. The feeder kicks to the central player.
3. As the football travels, the switch receiver begins moving towards the target cone.
4. The central player marks the football.
5. The central player opens the body towards the switch.
6. The central player delivers the football into the receiver’s running path.
7. The switch receiver marks while continuing forward.
8. Players rotate through all positions.
9. Reverse the switching direction after several minutes.
10. The receiver should not stop and wait underneath the football.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan the switch side before receiving.
Mark with the body ready to open.
Turn using short, balanced steps.
Identify the receiver’s speed and direction.
Kick to where the receiver is going.
Use appropriate height and weight.
Avoid floating the football unnecessarily.

commonErrors.error: Central player does not scan before receiving
commonErrors.correction: Check the switch side while the first kick is travelling.

commonErrors.error: Receiver begins the run too early
commonErrors.correction: Delay until the ball is moving towards the central player.

commonErrors.error: Switch kick travels behind the receiver
commonErrors.correction: Aim further into the running path.
Use a flatter trajectory where appropriate.

commonErrors.error: Central player takes too long to turn
commonErrors.correction: Prepare the body before completing the mark.

progressions: Add a player on the mark.
Allow the receiver to choose between two running lanes.
Require non-preferred foot use in one direction.
regressions: Tell the receiver when and where to move.
Allow the central player additional preparation time.
successIndicators: Allow the receiver to maintain momentum.
matchApplication: This drill develops switching play during: Defensive exits. Half-back ball movement. Wing transitions. Changes of attacking angle. Movement away from a congested side.
relatedDrills: KK-039 – Short Mark and Switch Kick

title: Long Switch Kick
objective: Develop the ability to execute a longer switch kick across the ground while maintaining accuracy and appropriate trajectory. Players learn to generate distance through controlled technique rather than sacrificing balance.
players:
Minimum: 6
Ideal: 8–16
Maximum: 20 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place one kicking position near one side of the ground.
• Create a large receiving target zone 35–50 metres away on the opposite side.
• Place a receiver inside the target zone.
• A feeder stands approximately 10 metres from the kicker.
• Players form lines at feeder, kicker and receiver positions.
• Adjust distance according to age and kicking capability.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The kicker scans the target zone.
2. The feeder passes to the kicker.
3. The kicker marks or gathers the football.
4. The kicker turns towards the opposite side.
5. The kicker uses a controlled approach.
6. The kicker delivers a long kick into the target zone.
7. The receiver marks or gathers.
8. Players rotate positions.
9. Practise switching in both directions.
10. Players score one point when the kick lands inside the target zone and two points when the receiver marks it.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Align the entire body with the target.
Use a smooth approach.
Maintain a controlled ball drop.
Generate power through leg speed and follow-through.
Avoid leaning backwards.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage.
Use enough height to clear pressure without allowing excessive hang time.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Difference between preferred and non-preferred directions.

commonErrors.correction: Keep the chest over the football and drive through the kick.

commonErrors.error: Kick has excessive height and little distance
commonErrors.correction: Improve contact and increase leg speed.
Align the hips and shoulders before the approach.
Reduce effort slightly and restore clean technique.

commonErrors.error: Receiver waits at the back of the zone
commonErrors.correction: Position to move towards the football.

progressions: Add a player on the mark.
regressions: Allow the kicker to begin with the football.
successIndicators: Land kicks inside the target zone.
Give the receiver a realistic marking opportunity.
matchApplication: Long switch kicks are used to: Move the football away from defensive congestion. Access the open side. Change the angle of attack. Exit defensive 50. Transfer play across half-back.
relatedDrills: KK-041 – Switch Kick to Moving Target

title: Defensive Exit Switch
objective: Develop the ability to switch the football from a defensive position when the direct side is congested. Players learn to recognise pressure, use a safe release option and move the football towards the open side.
setup:
• Create four positions:
• Defensive ball carrier near one boundary.
• Short central release target.
• Opposite-side switch target.
• Final outlet target further up the ground.
• Place one passive defender near the direct-side option to represent congestion.
• Players form lines at each attacking position.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The defensive ball carrier begins with the football.
2. The defender positions to discourage the direct kick.
3. The ball carrier scans the central and opposite-side options.
4. The ball carrier kicks to the short central release target.
5. The central player marks and immediately opens towards the opposite side.
6. The central player kicks to the switch target.
7. The switch target marks and delivers to the final outlet.
8. Players follow their disposals and rotate.
9. Repeat from the opposite boundary.
10. The drill should move the football away from pressure rather than through it.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Recognise when the direct side is blocked.
Use the safe release player.
Scan before receiving.
Position the body to continue the switch.
Maintain width.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage.
Move immediately after disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Initial decision by the defensive player.
Whether players force the direct option.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier forces the kick down the congested side
commonErrors.correction: Use the central release and switch away from pressure.

commonErrors.error: Central player receives with a closed body
commonErrors.correction: Position side-on and scan the far side before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Switch target moves too close to the centre
commonErrors.correction: Hold width to stretch the defensive shape.
Follow the football and support the next possession.
Prepare the next kick before receiving.

progressions: Allow defenders to adjust their positioning.
Add moving switch and outlet targets.
Continue into a live transition game.
successIndicators: Complete the switch before pressure recovers.
matchApplication: This drill replicates defensive ball movement when: One boundary is congested. The opposition has shifted across. A central release player is available. The open side can be accessed. A direct clearance would create a turnover risk.
relatedDrills: KK-039 – Short Mark and Switch Kick
KK-041 – Switch Kick to Moving Target

title: Switch, Run and Receive
primarySkill: Following a Switch to Receive Again
objective: Develop the ability to switch the football and immediately support the next phase of play. Players learn that a kick does not end their involvement and practise running to receive again in a new position.
players:
Minimum: 8
Ideal: 12–20
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create four positions in a wide diamond:
• Starting player.
• Central release.
• Wide switch target.
• Forward return target.
• Place the starting player and central release approximately 15 metres apart.
• Place the switch target 20–25 metres across the ground.
• Place the return target 15–20 metres ahead of the switch target.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A kicks to the central release.
2. Player A immediately begins a hard support run across and forward.
3. The central release marks and kicks to the wide switch target.
4. The switch target marks and looks inside.
5. Player A continues the support run into the return lane.
6. The switch target kicks to Player A.
7. Player A marks and delivers to the forward target.
8. Players rotate through each position.
9. Repeat in both directions.
10. The original kicker must time the support run so they arrive after the switch has been completed.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Move immediately after disposal.
Run with purpose rather than jogging.
Maintain a clear support angle.
Communicate during the run.
Scan while moving.
Kick to the runner’s advantage.
Avoid arriving too early and becoming stationary.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the runner arrives in space.

commonErrors.correction: Begin the support run immediately after disposal.
Delay slightly or use a wider running line.
Run across and forward into clear space.

commonErrors.error: Switch player does not scan inside
commonErrors.correction: Look for the returning runner before marking.

commonErrors.error: Final kick is rushed due to fatigue
commonErrors.correction: Control the final steps and maintain technique.

progressions: Add a second possible returning runner.
Add a time target for completing the chain.
Finish with a shot at goal.
successIndicators: Maintain kicking quality under physical load.
matchApplication: This drill develops repeat involvement during: Defensive switches. Half-back overlaps. Wing transitions. Give-and-go ball movement. Attacking chains through the corridor.
relatedDrills: KK-041 – Switch Kick to Moving Target

title: Corridor Transfer Kick
primarySkill: Transferring the Football into the Corridor
objective: Develop the ability to move the football from a wide position into a central corridor target. Players learn to recognise when the central option is available and deliver a firm, accurate kick that supports continued forward movement.
players:
Minimum: 8
Ideal: 12–20
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place one wide ball-carrier position near a boundary.
• Create a corridor gate approximately four to six metres wide, 20–25 metres infield.
• Position a central receiver beyond the gate.
• Place a forward target another 20 metres ahead.
• A passive defender begins near the corridor gate.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The wide ball carrier receives from a feeder.
2. The central receiver presents through the corridor gate.
3. The defender moves to either partially close or leave the corridor lane.
4. The ball carrier scans the defender and central receiver.
5. When the lane is available, the ball carrier kicks firmly through the gate.
6. The central receiver marks and turns forward.
7. The central receiver kicks to the forward target.
8. Players rotate positions.
9. If the corridor is closed, the ball carrier uses a designated safe outlet before the drill resets.
10. The drill should reward correct recognition rather than forcing every kick into the corridor.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan the central lane early.
Recognise whether the corridor is open.
Avoid forcing the kick when pressure has closed the lane.
Use a firm, direct trajectory.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage.
Prepare the central receiver to turn forward.
Maintain width when the corridor is unavailable.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Scanning by the wide ball carrier.
Decision to use or avoid the corridor.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier forces the corridor when closed
commonErrors.correction: Use the safe outlet and wait for a better opportunity.

commonErrors.error: Kick floats through the central lane
commonErrors.correction: Use a firmer, flatter trajectory.
Present actively through the gate.

commonErrors.error: Receiver marks with back to the forward target
commonErrors.correction: Position side-on and scan before receiving.
Scan centrally before looking down the boundary.

progressions: Use moving central and forward targets.
Continue into live play after the central mark.
regressions: Predetermine whether the lane is open.
successIndicators: Prepare the central receiver to continue forward.
matchApplication: Corridor transfer kicks can: Open the ground. Create faster forward movement. Move behind defensive pressure. Improve scoring opportunities. Change the point of attack.
relatedDrills: KK-039 – Short Mark and Switch Kick

title: Three-Kick Transition Chain
objective: Develop the ability to connect three consecutive kicks while moving the football from defence into attack. Players learn to prepare before receiving, maintain spacing and support the possession chain after disposal.
players:
Minimum: 10
Ideal: 14–22
Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create four stations extending from defence towards attack:
• Station A: Defensive start.
• Station B: Short outlet.
• Station C: Wide or central transition target.
• Station D: Forward target.
• Place each station 15–25 metres apart.
• Players form lines at all stations.
• Use a second football once the group understands the pattern.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A kicks to Player B.
2. Player A follows the disposal.
3. Player B scans, marks and turns towards Player C.
4. Player B kicks to Player C and follows.
5. Player C marks while moving or plays on immediately.
6. Player C kicks to Player D.
7. Player D marks and carries the football back along the outside of the drill.
8. All players rotate forward one station.
9. Continue for the allocated time.
10. Reverse the direction or change station angles.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan the next target before receiving.
Communicate early.
Kick to the receiver’s advantage.
Follow every disposal.
Maintain width and spacing.
Move the football quickly without rushing.
Adjust kicking weight for each distance.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the second football creates congestion.

commonErrors.error: Receiver watches only the incoming football
commonErrors.correction: Scan the next target before completing the mark.
Follow the disposal and support the chain.
Place the football into their path.
Increase station spacing or reduce football numbers.

commonErrors.error: Players rush to complete the chain
commonErrors.correction: Maintain technical quality before increasing speed.

progressions: Introduce moving targets at every station.
Add a decision between two targets.
Require non-preferred foot use at one station.
Finish with a shot at goal.
regressions: Walk through the pattern before increasing pace.
successIndicators: Maintain accuracy under increasing physical load.
matchApplication: This drill replicates transition ball movement through: Defensive exit. Half-back connection. Wing or corridor movement. Forward entry. Repeated support running.

title: Boundary-to-Corridor Transition
primarySkill: Moving the Football from Boundary to Corridor
objective: Develop the ability to move possession from a wide boundary position into the corridor through a controlled sequence of kicks. Players learn to recognise the correct moment to transfer infield and continue the transition forward.
players:
Minimum: 10
Ideal: 14–22
Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create four stations:
• Boundary starting position.
• Short boundary outlet.
• Central corridor receiver.
• Forward target.
• Place the boundary outlet 15–20 metres ahead of the starting position.
• Place the corridor receiver 20–25 metres infield from the boundary outlet.
• Place the forward target another 20–30 metres ahead.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. Player A begins with the football near the boundary.
2. Player A kicks to Player B at the short boundary outlet.
3. Player B scans the corridor before marking.
4. The passive defender adjusts position to either open or partially close the corridor.
5. If the corridor is open, Player B kicks to Player C infield.
6. Player C marks, turns forward and kicks to Player D.
7. If the corridor is closed, Player B uses a designated safe return option before the drill resets.
8. Players follow their disposals and rotate.
9. Repeat from both boundaries.
10. The drill should reward recognition rather than forcing the corridor kick every time.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Maintain width on the boundary.
Scan infield before receiving.
Recognise whether the corridor is open.
Use a firm, accurate transfer kick.
Avoid floating the football into pressure.
Position the corridor receiver side-on.
Turn forward immediately after the central mark.

commonErrors.error: Player forces the corridor when closed
commonErrors.correction: Use the safe option and retain possession.

commonErrors.error: Corridor receiver stands directly behind the defender
commonErrors.correction: Move into a clear diagonal passing lane.
Use a firmer and flatter trajectory.

commonErrors.error: Boundary player receives with no awareness
commonErrors.correction: Scan infield before the mark.
Follow the football and support the next phase.

regressions: Predetermine when the corridor is open.
successIndicators: Continue forward after entering the corridor.
matchApplication: This drill applies when teams: Exit defence along the boundary. Draw opponents towards one side. Transfer into the corridor. Create a more direct route to goal. Change from safe possession to attacking transition.

title: Corridor-to-Forward Entry
objective: Develop the ability to deliver an effective forward entry after receiving possession in the corridor. Players learn to scan multiple forward options, recognise space and kick to the leading player’s advantage.
players:
Minimum: 9
Ideal: 12–21
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place one corridor receiving position approximately 45–60 metres from goal or a designated scoring zone.
• Create three forward starting positions:
• Left lead.
• Central lead.
• Right lead.
• Position one passive defender between the corridor player and the forwards.
• A feeder stands 15 metres behind the corridor receiver.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The corridor player scans all three forward positions.
2. The feeder kicks to the corridor player.
3. As the football travels, the forwards begin their leads.
4. The defender moves to influence one of the options.
5. The corridor player marks, assesses the available space and selects a target.
6. The corridor player kicks to the chosen forward’s advantage.
7. The forward marks or gathers and completes a shot at goal or target kick.
8. Players rotate through corridor, forward, defender and feeder roles.
9. Continue for the allocated time.
10. The forward entries should vary rather than follow a fixed sequence.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan before receiving.
Identify forward spacing.
Avoid kicking to crowded areas.
Use the lead that creates the greatest separation.
Place the football into the receiver’s path.
Use a lower trajectory when the lane is clear.
Avoid overkicking the leading player.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Timing and spacing of forward leads.
Whether forwards lead into the same space.

commonErrors.error: All forwards lead to the same area
commonErrors.correction: Allocate different starting lanes and lead patterns.

commonErrors.error: Corridor player kicks to the loudest target
commonErrors.correction: Select the option with the best space and separation.

commonErrors.error: Kick goes over the forward’s head
commonErrors.correction: Reduce power and improve touch.

commonErrors.error: Player waits too long after marking
commonErrors.correction: Make the decision while the leads are developing.

commonErrors.error: Kick is placed directly at the defender
commonErrors.correction: Deliver into the open side of the lead.

progressions: Allow forwards to choose their own leads.
matchApplication: This drill replicates attacking possessions when players: Win the football through the corridor. Break a defensive line. Deliver inside 50. Select between several forward targets. Need to avoid an intercept defender.

title: Inside-50 Target Selection
objective: Develop the ability to select the most effective target when entering the forward 50. Players learn to compare multiple options, recognise dangerous space and avoid kicking automatically to a crowded contest.
players:
Minimum: 10
Ideal: 14–22
Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create one ball-carrier position outside forward 50.
• Set three forward options:
• Short lead.
• Deep lead.
• Lateral lead into space.
• Position two passive defenders to influence the available options.
• A feeder stands behind the ball carrier.
• Players form lines at all positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The ball carrier scans the forward structure.
2. The feeder delivers the football.
3. As the ball carrier receives, the three forwards begin different leads.
4. The defenders adjust to cover or influence selected options.
5. The ball carrier chooses the target that offers:
6. The greatest separation.
7. The safest kicking lane.
8. The strongest scoring opportunity.
9. The ball carrier delivers the football.
10. The selected forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan before possession.
Recognise the deepest dangerous option.
Use short leads when deep space is unavailable.
Avoid kicking to outnumbered contests.
Consider the defender’s position.
Kick to the forward’s advantage.
Maintain composure around forward 50.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players repeatedly choose the deepest option.
Whether decisions create realistic shots at goal.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier bombs to a crowded area
commonErrors.correction: Scan for short and lateral options.

commonErrors.error: Player chooses the first lead seen
commonErrors.correction: Compare all available options before committing.

commonErrors.error: Forwards lead into the same lane
commonErrors.correction: Maintain distinct leading patterns.
Place the football on the forward’s protected side.
Stay composed and use the best available option.

progressions: Continue into live play after the entry.
matchApplication: This drill develops decision making during one of the most important moments in Australian Football: the kick inside 50. It applies to: Fast entries. Slow possession entries. Entries from the corridor. Entries from the boundary. Rebound and turnover situations.
relatedDrills: KK-052 – Deep versus Short Entry Decision

title: Forward Entry to Space
objective: Develop the ability to kick into open forward space so a teammate can attack the football at speed. Players learn to place the ball away from defenders and avoid kicking directly to a stationary target.
players:
Minimum: 8
Ideal: 12–20
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place one ball-carrier position 40–55 metres from goal or a target area.
• Create three forward-entry zones:
• Left pocket space.
• Central space.
• Right pocket space.
• A forward begins behind the zones.
• A passive defender begins between the forward and ball carrier.
• A feeder stands behind the ball carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The ball carrier receives from the feeder.
2. The forward observes the defender’s position.
3. The forward leads towards the open target zone.
4. The ball carrier reads the lead.
5. The ball carrier kicks into the selected space.
6. The forward attacks the football at speed.
7. The forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
8. Players rotate roles.
9. Continue from different entry angles.
10. The football should be placed into space rather than directly onto the forward’s head unless the lead demands it.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Read the defender’s position.
Kick away from defensive pressure.
Use space in front of the forward.
Match kicking weight to the lead.
Keep the ball low enough to reduce defensive recovery time.
Avoid overkicking the target zone.
Allow the forward to maintain speed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the football remains inside the target area.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier kicks directly at the forward
commonErrors.correction: Place the football into the open space ahead.

commonErrors.error: Kick goes too close to the defender
commonErrors.correction: Target the forward’s protected side.
Reduce power and improve touch.
Attack the target zone at speed.
Use a flatter trajectory where the lane is clear.

progressions: Allow the forward to choose any zone.
successIndicators: Allow the forward to maintain speed.
matchApplication: Kicking to forward space is especially valuable when: The forward line is open. Defenders are positioned goal side. A teammate has speed advantage. Direct marking targets are unavailable. The team is attacking from turnover.
relatedDrills: KK-052 – Deep versus Short Entry Decision

title: Lowered-Eyes Forward Entry
objective: Develop the habit of lowering the eyes before entering forward 50 and identifying short or lateral targets rather than automatically kicking long to a contest.
players:
Minimum: 9
Ideal: 12–21
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place the ball carrier outside forward 50.
• Create:
• One deep forward target.
• Two short lead targets.
• One lateral target.
• Position one or two passive defenders near the deep option.
• A feeder stands 15 metres behind the ball carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The ball carrier scans the forward line before receiving.
2. The feeder passes to the ball carrier.
3. The deep forward and short targets begin their movements.
4. The defenders influence the deep option.
5. The ball carrier lowers the eyes and assesses the shorter targets.
6. The ball carrier selects the best available option.
7. The receiver marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
8. Players rotate through all roles.
9. Continue with different defensive positions.
10. The deep option remains available when it is genuinely the best choice.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan deep and short.
Avoid becoming fixed on the goal square.
Recognise defenders dropping back.
Reward short leads with separation.
Use controlled kicking weight.
Place the football in front of the receiver.
Remain patient while moving at speed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player scans short options.
Whether the player defaults to the deep kick.
Quality of the resulting scoring chance.

commonErrors.correction: Scan short targets before beginning the kicking action.
Begin the lead as the ball carrier receives.

commonErrors.error: Kick is too powerful for the short target
commonErrors.correction: Reduce force and use touch.

commonErrors.error: Player ignores an open lateral target
commonErrors.correction: Scan the full width of the forward line.

commonErrors.error: Deep target is used despite an outnumber
commonErrors.correction: Select the free short option.

progressions: Add a closing defender behind the ball carrier.
Allow defenders to cover short options.
regressions: Use one short and one deep target.
matchApplication: Lowered-eyes entries are important when: Defenders drop deep. The goal square is crowded. Short forwards create separation. A lateral option improves the scoring angle. Controlled possession is preferable to a contest.
relatedDrills: KK-052 – Deep versus Short Entry Decision
KK-053 – Forward Entry Under Chasing Pressure

title: Deep versus Short Entry Decision
primarySkill: Choosing Between Deep and Short Forward Entries
objective: Develop the ability to compare a deep attacking option with a shorter possession option and select the entry that creates the strongest scoring opportunity.
players:
Minimum: 9
Ideal: 12–21
Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
setup:
• Create:
• One ball-carrier position outside forward 50.
• One deep forward starting near goal.
• One short forward starting 25–35 metres from goal.
• One defender assigned to influence the deep option.
• One second defender positioned between the short and deep areas.
• A feeder stands behind the ball carrier.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The ball carrier scans both forward options.
2. The feeder passes to the ball carrier.
3. The deep and short forwards begin their leads.
4. The defenders adjust their positioning.
5. The ball carrier assesses:
6. Separation.
7. Defender numbers.
8. Kicking lane.
9. Likely scoring outcome.
10. The ball carrier selects either the deep or short option.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Scan before possession.
Compare the quality of both options.
Use the deep target when separation is clear.
Use the short option when defenders protect space behind.
Consider the likely shot location.
Avoid choosing by habit.
Weight each kick appropriately.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player repeatedly chooses one option.
Quality of the resulting shot at goal.

commonErrors.error: Player always chooses the deep target
commonErrors.correction: Compare defensive numbers and short separation.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier always chooses the easy short kick
commonErrors.correction: Use the deep option when it creates a stronger scoring chance.

commonErrors.error: Decision is made before defenders move
commonErrors.correction: Continue scanning as the leads develop.

commonErrors.error: Kick weight does not suit the selected target
commonErrors.correction: Adjust trajectory and power to the distance.
Separate the deep and short leading lanes.

matchApplication: This drill develops forward-entry decisions when: A deep forward has separation. Defenders drop behind the ball. A short lead presents inside 50. The ball carrier must choose between territory and possession. The quality of the next shot matters more than distance gained.
relatedDrills: KK-053 – Forward Entry Under Chasing Pressure
KK-054 – Forward Entry with Closing Defender

title: Forward Entry Under Chasing Pressure
objective: Develop the ability to deliver an effective forward entry while a defender applies pressure from behind. Players learn to accelerate into space, scan the forward line early and complete the kick before pressure forces a rushed disposal.
players:
Minimum: 10
Ideal: 14–22
Maximum: 28 using multiple groups
setup:
• Place:
• One ball-carrier starting cone 55–65 metres from goal.
• One chasing defender’s cone three to five metres behind.
• Three forward starting positions inside 50.
• Optional left, central and right target zones.
• The ball carrier begins with the football.
• The forwards begin in separate leading lanes.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. On the coach’s signal, the ball carrier and chasing defender begin.
2. The ball carrier accelerates towards forward 50.
3. The forwards begin their leads.
4. The ball carrier scans the available targets while running.
5. The defender closes from behind without tackling.
6. The ball carrier selects the best option and delivers before the defender reaches effective pressure.
7. The selected forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
8. Players rotate through ball-carrier, defender and forward roles.
9. Adjust the defender’s starting gap to suit the group.
10. The ball carrier should not wait until reaching the 50-metre line if a strong option appears earlier.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.

title: Forward Entry with Closing Defender
objective: Develop the ability to create and use a forward-entry kicking lane while a defender closes from the front. Players learn to recognise the defender’s line, make a small angle change and deliver into the forward 50 without kicking into smothering pressure.

Ideal: 14–22

1. The feeder passes to the ball carrier.
2. The defender closes from the front with hands raised.
3. The forwards begin leads through the two entry gates.
4. The ball carrier scans the defender and forward options.

Scan both entry lanes before receiving.
Recognise the defender’s closing line.
Use a small lateral movement.
Prepare the football early.
Avoid drifting too far sideways.
Select the forward away from pressure.
Maintain a compact and balanced kick.

Read the defender.

Use decisive footwork.

Select the best lead.

Control the final steps.

title: Kicking Possession Transition Game
objective: Develop the ability to retain possession through kicking and transition immediately when possession changes. Players learn to spread quickly in attack, close space in defence and make effective decisions during turnover moments.
setup:
• Create a rectangular playing area.
• Divide players into two teams.
• Recommended formats:
• Five versus five with two neutral players.
• Six versus six.
• Seven versus seven in a larger area.
• Neutral players, if used, always play with the team in possession.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The coach begins play with one team.
2. The team in possession retains the football using kicks.
3. One point is awarded for every five consecutive marks.
4. If possession changes, the new attacking team spreads immediately.
5. The team that lost possession transitions into defence.
6. Play continues without stopping after interceptions or loose-ball wins.
7. Restart only when the football leaves the area or becomes trapped.
8. Play for timed blocks.
9. Optional scoring:
10. Two points for five consecutive kicks followed by a successful switch.
coachingPoints: Focus on one coaching point at a time.
Spread immediately after winning possession.
Close space immediately after losing possession.
Scan before receiving.
Use short, accurate kicks.
Maintain width and depth.
Avoid kicking into central pressure.
Communicate during transition.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Decision making immediately after possession changes.
Whether players switch mentally between attack and defence.

commonErrors.correction: Close the nearest space immediately.

commonErrors.correction: Spread quickly to create kicking lanes.

commonErrors.correction: Secure possession and use the first safe option.

title: Zone-to-Zone Kicking Game

• Midfield zone.

howTheDrillWorks:
1. Play begins in one team’s defensive zone.
2. The team must progress the football through the midfield zone before entering the attacking zone.
3. Players may move between zones, but the coach may initially restrict numbers in each zone.
4. A point is scored when a player marks a kick inside the attacking end zone.
5. If possession changes, the new team attacks in the opposite direction.

7. Restart after scores or when the football leaves the area.
8. Play for timed blocks.

10. At least one kick must be completed in each zone.

title: Intercept Mark Transition Kick
objective: Develop the ability to take an intercept mark, scan immediately and launch an effective transition kick before the opposition can recover defensively.

setup:

• One attacking feeder outside a defensive zone.

• Short outlet.
• Wide switch.
• Central attacking option.
howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder kicks towards the intended attacking target.
2. The intercept defender reads the kick and moves to mark.
3. As the intercept occurs, the three transition targets move into their lanes.
4. The intercept player scans immediately.
5. The intercept player selects and completes the best transition kick.
6. The receiver marks and continues the possession to a final target.
7. Players rotate through feeder, attacker, interceptor and transition roles.
8. Vary the location and height of the initial kick.
9. The intercept player may play on or use a controlled kick from the mark.

Mark at the highest safe point.
Scan before landing where possible.

Avoid automatically kicking down the line.

title: Intercept and Switch

howTheDrillWorks:
1. The feeder kicks towards the intended target.
2. The intercept player marks or wins possession.
3. The short release and switch target move immediately.
4. The interceptor may:
5. Kick directly to the switch.

Recognise where the opposition has shifted.

Move before defensive recovery.

title: Defensive Zone Penetration Kick
objective: Develop the ability to identify and execute kicks that penetrate an organised defensive zone without exposing the team to high-risk turnovers.
setup:

• Position the defending team in an organised zone structure.

howTheDrillWorks:
1. The attacking team circulates possession to move the zone.
2. Players ahead of the football adjust their positioning to create passing lanes.
3. The ball carrier identifies whether to:
4. Kick through the zone.
5. Kick around the zone.
6. Retain possession.
7. Take territory to a contest.
8. Bonus points are awarded for penetrating through a gate and retaining possession.
9. The defending team attempts to intercept and counterattack.
10. Play continues until a score, turnover or successful exit.
coachingPoints: Move the zone before attempting penetration.
Scan through the defensive line rather than only around it.
Use sharp-angle kicks where safe.
Position receivers between defensive lines.
Avoid slow, floating passes through central space.
Accelerate after breaking one line.
Maintain options behind the ball.

Timing and trajectory of penetrating kicks.
Ability to recognise when penetration is unsafe.

title: Defensive Line-Breaking Kick

5. Bypass at least one defensive line.
6. Connect with a teammate.
7. Allow the team to retain attacking momentum.
8. The receiver plays on or quickly moves the football forward.
9. The defending team attempts to intercept and counterattack.
10. Play continues until the final target zone is reached or possession changes.
coachingPoints: Scan beyond the nearest option.
Ensure the receiver has separation.
Use the correct trajectory for the available lane.
Avoid forcing line-breaking kicks into organised numbers.
Run forward immediately after the kick.
Provide support on both sides of the receiver.
Recognise when a safer possession kick is required.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Forward support after the line break.
Team reaction when the kick is unavailable.

commonErrors.error: Player automatically selects the nearest option
commonErrors.correction: Scan beyond the first defensive line.

title: Advanced Kicking Scenario Assessment

7. Possession changes.
8. The allotted time expires.

10. Decision quality.
